Base class for settings, allowing values to be overridden by environment variables.
This is useful in production for secrets you do not wish to save in code, it plays nicely with docker(-compose),
Heroku and any 12 factor app design.
All the below attributes can be set via `model_config`.
_case_sensitive: Whether environment and CLI variable names should be read with case-sensitivity.
_nested_model_default_partial_update: Whether to allow partial updates on nested model default object fields.
_env_prefix: Prefix for all environment variables. Defaults to `None`.
_env_prefix_target: Targets to which `_env_prefix` is applied. Default: `variable`.
_env_file: The env file(s) to load settings values from. Defaults to `Path('')`, which
means that the value from `model_config['env_file']` should be used. You can also pass
`None` to indicate that environment variables should not be loaded from an env file.
_env_file_encoding: The env file encoding, e.g. `'latin-1'`. Defaults to `None`.
_env_file_depth: The number of parent directories of the current working directory to
search for the env file if it is not found there. Defaults to `0` (no search).
_env_ignore_empty: Ignore environment variables where the value is an empty string. Default to `False`.
_env_nested_delimiter: The nested env values delimiter. Defaults to `None`.
_env_nested_max_split: The nested env values maximum nesting. Defaults to `None`, which means no limit.
_env_parse_none_str: The env string value that should be parsed (e.g. "null", "void", "None", etc.)
into `None` type(None). Defaults to `None` type(None), which means no parsing should occur.
_env_parse_enums: Parse enum field names to values. Defaults to `None.`, which means no parsing should occur.
_cli_prog_name: The CLI program name to display in help text. Defaults to `None` if _cli_parse_args is `None`.
_cli_parse_args: The list of CLI arguments to parse. Defaults to None.
If set to `True`, defaults to sys.argv[1:].
_cli_settings_source: Override the default CLI settings source with a user defined instance. Defaults to None.
_cli_parse_none_str: The CLI string value that should be parsed (e.g. "null", "void", "None", etc.) into
`None` type(None). Defaults to _env_parse_none_str value if set. Otherwise, defaults to "null" if
_cli_hide_none_type: Hide `None` values in CLI help text. Defaults to `False`.
_cli_avoid_json: Avoid complex JSON objects in CLI help text. Defaults to `False`.

Source class for loading settings values from CLI.
A `CliSettingsSource` connects with a `root_parser` object by using the parser methods to add
`settings_cls` fields as command line arguments. The `CliSettingsSource` internal parser representation
is based upon the `argparse` parsing library, and therefore, requires the parser methods to support
the same attributes as their `argparse` library counterparts.
cli_prog_name: The CLI program name to display in help text. Defaults to `None` if cli_parse_args is `None`.
cli_parse_args: The list of CLI arguments to parse. Defaults to None.
If set to `True`, defaults to sys.argv[1:].
cli_parse_none_str: The CLI string value that should be parsed (e.g. "null", "void", "None", etc.) into `None`
type(None). Defaults to "null" if cli_avoid_json is `False`, and "None" if cli_avoid_json is `True`.
cli_hide_none_type: Hide `None` values in CLI help text. Defaults to `False`.
cli_avoid_json: Avoid complex JSON objects in CLI help text. Defaults to `False`.
cli_enforce_required: Enforce required fields at the CLI. Defaults to `False`.
cli_use_class_docs_for_groups: Use class docstrings in CLI group help text instead of field descriptions.
cli_show_env_vars: Show resolved environment variable names in CLI help text. Defaults to `False`.
cli_exit_on_error: Determines whether or not the internal parser exits with error info when an error occurs.
cli_prefix: Prefix for command line arguments added under the root parser. Defaults to "".
cli_flag_prefix_char: The flag prefix character to use for CLI optional arguments. Defaults to '-'.
cli_implicit_flags: Controls how `bool` fields are exposed as CLI flags.
- False (default): no implicit flags are generated; booleans must be set explicitly (e.g. --flag=true).
- True / 'dual': optional boolean fields generate both positive and negative forms (--flag and --no-flag).
- 'toggle': required boolean fields remain in 'dual' mode, while optional boolean fields generate a single
flag aligned with the default value (if default=False, expose --flag; if default=True, expose --no-flag).
cli_ignore_unknown_args: Whether to ignore unknown CLI args and parse only known ones. Defaults to `False`.
cli_kebab_case: CLI args use kebab case. Defaults to `False`.
cli_shortcuts: Mapping of target field name to alias names. Defaults to `None`.

Pydantic settings supports running asynchronous CLI commands via `CliApp.run` and `CliApp.run_subcommand`. With this feature, you can define async def methods within your Pydantic models (including subcommands) and have them executed just like their synchronous counterparts. Specifically:
1. Asynchronous methods are supported: You can now mark your cli_cmd or similar CLI entrypoint methods as async def and have CliApp execute them.
2. Subcommands may also be asynchronous: If you have nested CLI subcommands, the final (lowest-level) subcommand methods can likewise be asynchronous.

3. Limit asynchronous methods to final subcommands: Defining parent commands as asynchronous is not recommended, because it can result in additional threads and event loops being created. For best performance and to avoid unnecessary resource usage, only implement your deepest (child) subcommands as async def.
Below is a simple example demonstrating an asynchronous top-level command:
print('Hello from an async CLI method!')
#> Hello from an async CLI method!
# If an event loop is already running, a new thread will be used;
# otherwise, asyncio.run() is used to execute this async method.

As mentioned above, you can also define subcommands as async. However, only do so for the leaf (lowest-level) subcommand to avoid spawning new threads and event loops unnecessarily in parent commands:
# Perform async tasks here, e.g. network or I/O operations
# Run the final subcommand (clone/init). It is recommended to define async methods only at the deepest level.

When executing a subcommand with an asynchronous cli_cmd, Pydantic settings automatically detects whether the current thread already has an active event loop. If so, the async command is run in a fresh thread to avoid conflicts. Otherwise, it uses asyncio.run() in the current thread. This handling ensures your asynchronous subcommands "just work" without additional manual setup.

You may set the following parameters:

All parameters below `ssm_path` are read recursively with the [`get_parameters_by_path`](https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/services/ssm/client/get_parameters_by_path.html)

For example, a parameter named `/prod/my-app/sub/a` populates the `a` field of the `sub` model. You must have the same
naming convention in the field name as in the parameter name, or use an alias.

The Azure Key Vault source accepts a `snake_case_conversion` option, disabled by default, to convert Key Vault secret names by mapping them to Python's snake_case field names, without the need to use aliases.
This setup will load Azure Key Vault secrets (e.g., `MySetting`, `mySetting`, `my-secret` or `MY-SECRET`), mapping them to the snake case version (`my_setting` in this case).

The Azure Key Vault source accepts a `dash_to_underscore` option, disabled by default, to support Key Vault kebab-case secret names by mapping them to Python's snake_case field names. When enabled, dashes (`-`) in secret names are mapped to underscores (`_`) in field names during validation.
This mapping applies only to *field names*, not to aliases. Use `--` to separate nested model fields; dashes in their names are mapped the same way, while dictionary keys are kept as-is.

This setup will load Azure Key Vault secrets named `field-with-underscore`, `Alias-With-Dashes` and `database--sql-password`, mapping them to the `field_with_underscore`, `field_with_alias` and `database.sql_password` fields, respectively.
Alternatively, you can configure an [alias_generator](alias.md#using-alias-generators) to map PascalCase secrets.

For example, if your settings model has `gcp_project: str = Field(alias='GCP_PROJECT')`, use `project_id_field='GCP_PROJECT'` (the alias), not `'gcp_project'` (the Python attribute name).

*   If you set `case_sensitive=False`, `pydantic-settings` will attempt to resolve secrets in a case-insensitive manner. It prioritizes exact matches over case-insensitive matches. For some examples of this, imagine `case_sensitive=False` and the model attribute is named `my_secret`:
* If Google Secret Manager has both `MY_SECRET` and `my_secret` defined - the value of `my_secret` will be returned.

* If Google Secret Manager has `MY_SECRET`, `My_Secret`, and `my_Secret` defined - a warning will be raised and the value of `my_Secret` will be returned - as the secret names are first sorted in ASCII sort order (where lowercased letters are greater than upper case letters) and the last one is chosen (which would be `my_Secret` in this case).

2. **Secret Naming**: Create secrets in Google Secret Manager with names that match your field names (including any prefix). 36|def _warn_if_field_info_incomplete(field_info: FieldInfo, field_name: str, init_state: InitState) -> None:
37|    """Warn if the field is incomplete, i.e. its annotation contains unresolved forward references.
38|
39|    An incomplete `FieldInfo` instance is unsafe to inspect — any of its attributes (annotation,
40|    aliases, metadata, default) may rely on the unresolved annotation, so settings sources may
41|    silently fail to resolve the field's value. Each instance is only warned about once per
42|    `init_state`, so that a field accessed by multiple sources during a single settings
43|    resolution doesn't emit duplicate warnings.
44|    """
45|    if getattr(field_info, '_complete', True):
46|        return
47|    warned_ids = init_state.setdefault('field_info_ids', set())
48|    if id(field_info) in warned_ids:
49|        return
50|    warned_ids.add(id(field_info))
51|    warnings.warn(  # noqa: B028  (called from many sources at differing depths, so no stacklevel is correct)
52|        f'Field {field_name!r} has an incomplete definition: its annotation contains an unresolved '
53|        'forward reference, so settings sources may fail to correctly resolve its value. '
54|        'Call `model_rebuild()` on the model where the field is defined, once all the referenced '
55|        'types are defined.',
56|        IncompleteFieldDefinitionWarning,
57|    )

100|def _substitute_typevars(tp: Any, param_map: dict[Any, Any]) -> Any:
101|    """Substitute TypeVars in a type annotation with concrete types from param_map."""
102|    if isinstance(tp, TypeVar) and tp in param_map:
103|        return param_map[tp]
104|    args = get_args(tp)
105|    if not args:
106|        return tp
107|    new_args = tuple(_substitute_typevars(arg, param_map) for arg in args)
108|    if new_args == args:
109|        return tp
110|    origin = get_origin(tp)
111|    if origin is not None:
112|        try:
113|            return origin[new_args]
114|        except TypeError:
115|            # types.UnionType and similar are not directly subscriptable,
116|            # reconstruct using | operator
117|            import functools
118|            import operator
119|
120|            return functools.reduce(operator.or_, new_args)
121|    # Unreachable in practice: an annotation with args always has an origin.
122|    # Kept as a defensive fallback.
123|    return tp  # pragma: no cover

126|def _resolve_type_alias(annotation: Any) -> Any:
127|    """Resolve a TypeAliasType to its underlying value, substituting type params if parameterized.
128|
129|    Aliases of aliases are followed until a non-alias annotation is reached. This terminates because
130|    pydantic rejects aliases that circularly refer to themselves without going through another type.
131|    """
132|    while True:
133|        if typing_objects.is_typealiastype(annotation):
134|            annotation = annotation.__value__
135|            continue
136|        origin = get_origin(annotation)
137|        if not typing_objects.is_typealiastype(origin):
138|            return annotation
139|        type_params = getattr(origin, '__type_params__', ())
140|        type_args = get_args(annotation)
141|        annotation = origin.__value__
142|        # Always true in practice: only a subscripted alias reaches here, and subscripting
143|        # requires type params.
144|        if type_params and type_args:  # pragma: no branch
145|            # Not `strict=True`: a parameterized alias may supply fewer args than
146|            # params (e.g. type params with defaults), which is valid.
147|            annotation = _substitute_typevars(annotation, dict(zip(type_params, type_args, strict=False)))

150|def _annotation_is_complex(annotation: Any, metadata: list[Any], init_state: InitState | None = None) -> bool:
151|    # If the model is a root model, the root annotation should be used to
152|    # evaluate the complexity.
153|    annotation = _resolve_type_alias(annotation)
154|    if annotation is not None and _lenient_issubclass(annotation, RootModel) and annotation is not RootModel:
155|        annotation = cast('type[RootModel[Any]]', annotation)
156|        root_field = annotation.model_fields['root']
157|        if init_state is not None:
158|            _warn_if_field_info_incomplete(root_field, f'{annotation.__name__}.root', init_state)
159|        root_annotation = root_field.annotation
160|        if root_annotation is not None:  # pragma: no branch
161|            annotation = root_annotation
162|
163|    if any(isinstance(md, Json) for md in metadata):  # type: ignore[misc]
164|        return False
165|
166|    origin = get_origin(annotation)
167|
168|    # Check if annotation is of the form Annotated[type, metadata].
169|    if typing_objects.is_annotated(origin):
170|        # Return result of recursive call on inner type.
171|        inner, *meta = get_args(annotation)
172|        return _annotation_is_complex(inner, meta, init_state)
173|
174|    if _lenient_issubclass(origin, Secret):
175|        return False
176|
177|    return (
178|        _annotation_is_complex_inner(annotation)
179|        or _annotation_is_complex_inner(origin)
180|        or hasattr(origin, '__pydantic_core_schema__')
181|        or hasattr(origin, '__get_pydantic_core_schema__')

213|def _union_is_complex(
214|    annotation: type[Any] | None,
215|    metadata: list[Any],
216|    init_state: InitState | None = None,
217|    _seen: tuple[Any, ...] = (),
218|) -> bool:
219|    """Check if a union type contains any complex types."""
220|    for arg in get_args(annotation):
221|        if arg in _seen:
222|            continue

224|        # but aliases with the same origin and arguments still compare equal.
225|        seen = (*_seen, arg)
226|        arg = _resolve_type_alias(arg)
227|        if _annotation_is_complex(arg, metadata, init_state):
228|            return True
229|        # _annotation_is_complex doesn't handle bare Union types, including those
230|        # exposed by a type alias or Annotated[Union[X, Y], ...]. Recurse, but only
231|        # if no Annotated metadata suppresses complexity (e.g. Json).
232|        inner = _unwrap_union_member(arg)
233|        if is_union_origin(get_origin(inner)) and _union_is_complex(inner, metadata, init_state, seen):
234|            return True

270|def _annotation_contains_types(
271|    annotation: Any,
272|    types: tuple[Any, ...],
273|    is_include_origin: bool = True,
274|    is_strip_annotated: bool = False,
275|    is_instance: bool = False,
276|    collect: set[Any] | None = None,
277|    is_subtype: bool = False,
278|    _seen_aliases: tuple[Any, ...] = (),
279|) -> bool:
280|    """Check if a type annotation contains any of the specified types.
281|
282|    With `is_subtype`, subclasses of the specified types match as well, so `tuple` matches
283|    `Sequence`, or `frozenset` matches `Set`.
284|    """
285|    if is_strip_annotated:
286|        annotation = _strip_annotated(annotation)
287|    resolved = _resolve_type_alias(annotation)
288|    if resolved is not annotation:
289|        # An alias already on the current path is recursive, so stop there. Only the current path is
290|        # tracked, so sibling specializations of the same alias are still inspected.
291|        return annotation not in _seen_aliases and _annotation_contains_types(
292|            resolved,
293|            types,
294|            is_include_origin=is_include_origin,
295|            is_strip_annotated=is_strip_annotated,
296|            is_instance=is_instance,
297|            collect=collect,
298|            is_subtype=is_subtype,
299|            _seen_aliases=(*_seen_aliases, annotation),
300|        )
301|    if is_include_origin is True:
302|        origin = get_origin(annotation)
303|        if origin in types or (is_subtype and _is_subtype_of(origin, types)):
304|            if collect is None:
305|                return True
306|            collect.add(annotation)
307|        if is_instance and any(isinstance(origin, type_) for type_ in types):
308|            if collect is None:
309|                return True
310|            collect.add(annotation)
311|    for type_ in get_args(annotation):
312|        if (
313|            _annotation_contains_types(
314|                type_,
315|                types,
316|                is_include_origin=True,
317|                is_strip_annotated=is_strip_annotated,
318|                is_instance=is_instance,
319|                collect=collect,
320|                is_subtype=is_subtype,
321|                _seen_aliases=_seen_aliases,
322|            )
323|            and collect is None
324|        ):
325|            return True
326|    if is_instance and any(isinstance(annotation, type_) for type_ in types):
327|        if collect is None:
328|            return True
329|        collect.add(annotation)
330|    if annotation in types or (is_subtype and _is_subtype_of(annotation, types)):
331|        if collect is not None:
332|            collect.add(annotation)
333|        return True
334|    return False

384|    if typing_objects.is_literal(get_origin(annotation)):

406|def _get_alias_names(
407|    field_name: str,
408|    field_info: FieldInfo,
409|    alias_path_args: dict[str, int | None] | None = None,
410|    case_sensitive: bool = True,
411|    populate_by_name: bool = False,
412|    validate_by_alias: bool = True,
413|) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], bool]:
414|    """Get alias names for a field, handling alias paths and case sensitivity.
415|
416|    With `validate_by_alias=False` pydantic ignores the aliases, so only the field name is returned.
417|
418|    The first name is the key that sources pass the value to pydantic under.
419|    """
420|    from pydantic import AliasChoices, AliasPath
421|
422|    alias_names: list[str] = []
423|    is_alias_path_only: bool = True
424|    if not validate_by_alias or not any((field_info.alias, field_info.validation_alias)):
425|        alias_names += [field_name]
426|        is_alias_path_only = False
427|    else:
428|        new_alias_paths: list[AliasPath] = []
429|        # Pydantic only validates input against `validation_alias` when it is set, so `alias` isn't an input name then
430|        alias = field_info.validation_alias if field_info.validation_alias is not None else field_info.alias
431|        if isinstance(alias, str):
432|            alias_names.append(alias)
433|            is_alias_path_only = False
434|        elif isinstance(alias, AliasChoices):
435|            for name in alias.choices:
436|                if isinstance(name, str):
437|                    alias_names.append(name)
438|                    is_alias_path_only = False
439|                else:
440|                    new_alias_paths.append(name)
441|        else:
442|            # Can't be `None`, the check above ensures one of the aliases is set
443|            new_alias_paths.append(cast(AliasPath, alias))
444|        for alias_path in new_alias_paths:
445|            name = cast(str, alias_path.path[0])
446|            name = name.lower() if not case_sensitive else name
447|            if alias_path_args is not None:
448|                alias_path_args[name] = (
449|                    alias_path.path[1] if len(alias_path.path) > 1 and isinstance(alias_path.path[1], int) else None
450|                )
451|            if not alias_names and is_alias_path_only:
452|                alias_names.append(name)
453|        if populate_by_name and field_name not in alias_names:
454|            alias_names.append(field_name)
455|            is_alias_path_only = False
456|    if not case_sensitive:
457|        alias_names = [alias_name.lower() for alias_name in alias_names]
458|    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(alias_names)), is_alias_path_only

294|    @classmethod
295|    def settings_cached(cls) -> Self:
296|        """Return the cached default settings instance for this settings class.
297|
298|        The instance is constructed on first use and reused afterwards. Subclasses are cached
299|        separately, so caching a class does not affect its parents or children.
300|        """
301|        with _settings_cache_guard:
302|            settings = _settings_cache.get(cls)
303|            if settings is not None:
304|                return cast(Self, settings)
305|            lock = _settings_cache_locks.get(cls)
306|            if lock is None:
307|                lock = _settings_cache_locks.setdefault(cls, threading.Lock())
308|
309|        # The settings are constructed without holding `_settings_cache_guard` so that sources
310|        # which wait on other threads, e.g. cloud secret managers, cannot deadlock the cache,
311|        # and so that unrelated settings classes can be loaded concurrently. The per-class lock
312|        # keeps a class from being built more than once.
313|        with lock:
314|            with _settings_cache_guard:
315|                settings = _settings_cache.get(cls)
316|            if settings is None:
317|                settings = cls()
318|                with _settings_cache_guard:
319|                    _settings_cache[cls] = settings
320|            return cast(Self, settings)

322|    @classmethod
323|    def settings_clear_cache(cls) -> None:
324|        """Remove the cached default settings instance for this settings class, if any.
325|
326|        Only the cache entry for this exact class is removed. Subclasses keep their own cached
327|        instances and must be cleared individually.
328|
329|        A `settings_cached()` call already in flight may still return the instance it was
330|        building, so clearing does not retroactively invalidate references other threads hold.
331|        """
332|        with _settings_cache_guard:
333|            _settings_cache.pop(cls, None)

558|    @classmethod
559|    def _settings_build_values(
560|        cls, sources: tuple[PydanticBaseSettingsSource, ...], init_kwargs: dict[str, Any]
561|    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
562|        if sources:
563|            state: dict[str, Any] = {}
564|            defaults: dict[str, Any] = {}
565|            states: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
566|            for source in sources:
567|                if isinstance(source, PydanticBaseSettingsSource):
568|                    source._set_current_state(state)
569|                    source._set_settings_sources_data(states)
570|
571|                source_name = source.__name__ if hasattr(source, '__name__') else type(source).__name__
572|                source_state = source()
573|
574|                if isinstance(source, DefaultSettingsSource):
575|                    defaults = source_state
576|
577|                states[source_name] = source_state
578|                state = deep_update(source_state, state)
579|
580|            # Strip any default values not explicitly set before returning final state
581|            state = {key: val for key, val in state.items() if key not in defaults or defaults[key] != val}
582|
583|            if _settings_debug_enabled() and logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
584|                cls._settings_log_debug(states)
585|            # The last source is the `DefaultSettingsSource` instance created in `_settings_init_sources()`,
586|            # holding the init state shared by all built-in sources:
587|            last_source = sources[-1]
588|            init_state = last_source._init_state if isinstance(last_source, PydanticBaseSettingsSource) else InitState()
589|            cls._settings_restore_init_kwarg_names(cls, init_kwargs, state, init_state)
590|
591|            return state
592|        # no one should mean to do this, but I think returning an empty dict is marginally preferable
593|        # to an informative error and much better than a confusing error
594|        return {}

596|    @classmethod
597|    def _settings_log_debug(cls, states: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
598|        """Log the data collected by each settings source in priority order.
599|
600|        Enabled by setting the ``PYDANTIC_SETTINGS_DEBUG`` environment variable to a truthy value.
601|        This is emitted at ``DEBUG`` level on the ``pydantic_settings`` logger.
602|
603|        Warning: the output may contain sensitive values loaded from the environment, dotenv
604|        files, or secret files. Only enable it in a trusted debugging context.
605|        """
606|        lines = [f'Resolving settings for {cls.__name__!r} (sources in priority order, highest first):']
607|        for name, source_state in states.items():
608|            lines.append(f'  {name}: {source_state!r}')
609|        logger.debug('\n'.join(lines))

611|    @staticmethod
612|    def _settings_restore_init_kwarg_names(
613|        settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
614|        init_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
615|        state: dict[str, Any],
616|        init_state: InitState,
617|    ) -> None:
618|        """
619|        Restore the init_kwarg key names to the final merged state dictionary.
620|
621|        This function renames keys in state to match the original init_kwargs key names,
622|        preserving the merged values from the source priority order.
623|        """
624|        if init_kwargs and state:
625|            state_kwarg_names = set(state.keys())
626|            init_kwarg_names = set(init_kwargs.keys())
627|            validate_by_alias = _validate_by_alias_enabled(settings_cls.model_config)
628|            for field_name, field_info in settings_cls.model_fields.items():
629|                _warn_if_field_info_incomplete(field_info, field_name, init_state)
630|                alias_names, *_ = _get_alias_names(field_name, field_info, validate_by_alias=validate_by_alias)
631|                matchable_names = set(alias_names)
632|                if _validate_by_name_enabled(settings_cls.model_config):
633|                    matchable_names.add(field_name)
634|                init_kwarg_name = init_kwarg_names & matchable_names
635|                state_kwarg_name = state_kwarg_names & matchable_names
636|                if init_kwarg_name and state_kwarg_name:
637|                    # Use deterministic selection for both keys.
638|                    # Target key: the key from init_kwargs that should be used in the final state.
639|                    target_key = next(iter(init_kwarg_name))
640|                    # Source key: prefer the alias (first in alias_names) if present in state,
641|                    # as InitSettingsSource normalizes to the preferred alias.
642|                    # This ensures we get the highest-priority value for this field.
643|                    source_key = next((alias for alias in alias_names if alias in state_kwarg_name), None)
644|                    if source_key is None:  # pragma: no cover
645|                        # Unreachable in practice: `InitSettingsSource` normalizes every matched
646|                        # init kwarg to the preferred alias, so when `init_kwarg_name` is non-empty
647|                        # that alias is always present in the state. Kept as a defensive fallback.
648|                        source_key = field_name if field_name in state_kwarg_name else next(iter(state_kwarg_name))
649|                    # Get the value from the source key and remove all matching keys
650|                    value = state.pop(source_key)
651|                    for key in state_kwarg_name - {source_key}:
652|                        state.pop(key, None)
653|                    state[target_key] = value

663|        Args:
664|            sources: The tuple of configured sources

101|    def get_field_value(self, field: FieldInfo, field_name: str) -> tuple[Any, str, bool]:
102|        """
103|        Gets the value for field from environment variables and a flag to determine whether value is complex.
104|
105|        Args:
106|            field: The field.
107|            field_name: The field name.
108|
109|        Returns:

111|                a flag to determine whether value is complex.
112|        """

114|        env_val: str | None = None

116|        # "unused loop variable" report doesn't apply here.
117|        for field_key, env_name, value_is_complex in self._extract_field_info(field, field_name):  # noqa: B007
118|            env_val = self.env_vars.get(env_name)

124|    def prepare_field_value(self, field_name: str, field: FieldInfo, value: Any, value_is_complex: bool) -> Any:
125|        """
126|        Prepare value for the field.
127|
128|        * Extract value for nested field.
129|        * Deserialize value to python object for complex field.
130|
131|        Args:
132|            field: The field.
133|            field_name: The field name.
134|
135|        Returns:
136|            A tuple contains prepared value for the field.
137|
138|        Raises:
139|            ValuesError: When There is an error in deserializing value for complex field.
140|        """
141|        is_complex, allow_parse_failure = self._field_is_complex(field)
142|        if self.env_parse_enums:
143|            enum_val = _annotation_enum_name_to_val(field.annotation, value)
144|            value = value if enum_val is None else enum_val

152|                if env_val_built:

156|                try:

172|    def _matches_alias_path_head(self, field: FieldInfo | Any | None, key: str) -> bool:
173|        """
174|        Whether ``key`` matches the first element of a multi-part ``AliasPath`` on ``field``.
175|
176|        When a nested field is aliased via e.g. ``AliasPath('path', 0)``, the env value found
177|        under ``path`` is a container that must be JSON-decoded before pydantic can navigate
178|        into it (see #670). This mirrors the complexity that ``_extract_field_info`` already
179|        reports for top-level ``AliasPath`` fields.
180|
181|        Args:
182|            field: The field (or raw type) matched for ``key``.
183|            key: The (case-normalized) env name segment matched for the field.
184|
185|        Returns:
186|            Whether ``key`` is the head of a multi-element ``AliasPath``.
187|        """
188|        if not isinstance(field, FieldInfo):
189|            return False
190|        v_alias = field.validation_alias
191|        paths: list[tuple[str | int, ...]] = []
192|        if isinstance(v_alias, AliasPath):
193|            paths.append(tuple(v_alias.path))
194|        elif isinstance(v_alias, AliasChoices):
195|            paths.extend(tuple(choice.path) for choice in v_alias.choices if isinstance(choice, AliasPath))
196|        for path in paths:
197|            head = path[0]
198|            if len(path) > 1 and isinstance(head, str) and self._apply_case_sensitive(head) == key:
199|                return True
200|        return False

202|    def _field_is_complex(self, field: FieldInfo) -> tuple[bool, bool]:

207|        if self.field_is_complex(field):
208|            allow_parse_failure = False
209|        elif is_union_origin(get_origin(annotation)) and _union_is_complex(annotation, metadata, self._init_state):
210|            allow_parse_failure = True

216|    def _raw_union_is_complex(self, annotation: Any) -> bool:
217|        """
218|        Find out if a raw type (e.g. a dict value type) is a union containing complex types.
219|        """

223|    def _decode_union_value(self, field_name: str, field: FieldInfo, value: str) -> Any:
224|        """
225|        Decode a value whose raw type is a union containing complex types, e.g. `list[str] | str`.
226|
227|        Only JSON arrays and objects are used, any other value is kept as the original string so that
228|        values like `123` or `true` still validate against the scalar members of the union.
229|        Decoding follows the `NoDecode`/`ForceDecode` metadata of the containing `field` and the
230|        `enable_decoding` config.
231|        """
232|        try:
233|            decoded = self.decode_complex_value(field_name, field, value)
234|        except ValueError:
235|            return value
236|        return decoded if isinstance(decoded, (list, dict)) else value

238|    # Default value of `case_sensitive` is `None`, because we don't want to break existing behavior.
239|    # We have to change the method to a non-static method and use

241|    def next_field(
242|        self, field: FieldInfo | Any | None, key: str, case_sensitive: bool | None = None
243|    ) -> FieldInfo | None:
244|        """
245|        Find the field in a sub model by key(env name)
246|
247|        By having the following models:
248|
249|            ```py
250|            class SubSubModel(BaseSettings):
251|                dvals: Dict
252|
253|            class SubModel(BaseSettings):
254|                vals: list[str]
255|                sub_sub_model: SubSubModel
256|
257|            class Cfg(BaseSettings):
258|                sub_model: SubModel
259|            ```
260|
261|        Then:
262|            next_field(sub_model, 'vals') Returns the `vals` field of `SubModel` class
263|            next_field(sub_model, 'sub_sub_model') Returns `sub_sub_model` field of `SubModel` class
264|
265|        Args:
266|            field: The field.
267|            key: The key (env name).
268|            case_sensitive: Whether to search for key case sensitively.
269|
270|        Returns:
271|            Field if it finds the next field otherwise `None`.
272|        """
273|        if not field:
274|            return None
275|
276|        annotation = field.annotation if isinstance(field, FieldInfo) else field
277|        for type_ in get_args(annotation):
278|            type_has_key = self.next_field(type_, key, case_sensitive)
279|            if type_has_key:
280|                return type_has_key
281|        if _lenient_issubclass(get_origin(annotation), dict):
282|            # get value type if it's a dict
283|            args = get_args(annotation)
284|            return args[-1] if args else None
285|        if is_model_class(annotation) or is_pydantic_dataclass(annotation):  # type: ignore[arg-type]
286|            fields = _get_model_fields(annotation)
287|            model_config = _get_model_config(annotation)
288|            # `case_sensitive is None` is here to be compatible with the old behavior.
289|            # Has to be removed in V3.
290|            for field_name, f in fields.items():
291|                for _, env_name, _ in self._extract_field_info(f, field_name, model_config):
292|                    if case_sensitive is None or case_sensitive:
293|                        if field_name == key or env_name == key:
294|                            return f
295|                    elif field_name.lower() == key.lower() or env_name.lower() == key.lower():
296|                        return f
297|        return None

299|    def explode_env_vars(self, field_name: str, field: FieldInfo, env_vars: Mapping[str, str | None]) -> dict[str, Any]:  # noqa: C901
300|        """
301|        Process env_vars and extract the values of keys containing env_nested_delimiter into nested dictionaries.
302|
303|        This is applied to a single field, hence filtering by env_var prefix.
304|
305|        Args:
306|            field_name: The field name.
307|            field: The field.
308|            env_vars: Environment variables.
309|
310|        Returns:
311|            A dictionary contains extracted values from nested env values.
312|        """
313|        if not self.env_nested_delimiter:
314|            return {}
315|
316|        ann = field.annotation
317|        is_dict = ann is dict or _lenient_issubclass(get_origin(ann), dict)
318|
319|        prefixes = [
320|            f'{env_name}{self.env_nested_delimiter}' for _, env_name, _ in self._extract_field_info(field, field_name)
321|        ]
322|        result: dict[str, Any] = {}
323|        for env_name, env_val in env_vars.items():
324|            try:
325|                prefix = next(prefix for prefix in prefixes if env_name.startswith(prefix))
326|            except StopIteration:
327|                continue
328|            # we remove the prefix before splitting in case the prefix has characters in common with the delimiter
329|            env_name_without_prefix = env_name[len(prefix) :]
330|            *keys, last_key = env_name_without_prefix.split(self.env_nested_delimiter, self.maxsplit)
331|            env_var = result
332|            target_field: FieldInfo | None = field
333|            # the closest field containing the target, its decoding settings apply to raw types
334|            parent_field = field
335|            for key in keys:
336|                target_field = self.next_field(target_field, key, self.case_sensitive)
337|                if isinstance(target_field, FieldInfo):
338|                    parent_field = target_field
339|                if isinstance(env_var, dict):
340|                    env_var = env_var.setdefault(key, {})
341|
342|            # get proper field with last_key
343|            target_field = self.next_field(target_field, last_key, self.case_sensitive)
344|
345|            # check if env_val maps to a complex field and if so, parse the env_val
346|            if (target_field or is_dict) and env_val:
347|                if isinstance(target_field, FieldInfo):
348|                    is_complex, allow_json_failure = self._field_is_complex(target_field)
349|                    if not is_complex and self._matches_alias_path_head(target_field, last_key):
350|                        # The env value sits under an AliasPath head (e.g. AliasPath('path', 0));
351|                        # decode it so pydantic can navigate into the container (see #670).
352|                        is_complex, allow_json_failure = True, True
353|                    if self.env_parse_enums:
354|                        enum_val = _annotation_enum_name_to_val(target_field.annotation, env_val)
355|                        env_val = env_val if enum_val is None else enum_val
356|                elif target_field:
357|                    # target_field is a raw type (e.g. from dict value type annotation)
358|                    is_complex = _annotation_is_complex(target_field, [], self._init_state)
359|                    allow_json_failure = True
360|                    if not is_complex and self._raw_union_is_complex(target_field):
361|                        env_val = self._decode_union_value(last_key, parent_field, env_val)
362|                else:
363|                    # nested field type is dict
364|                    is_complex, allow_json_failure = True, True
365|                if is_complex:
366|                    try:
367|                        field_info = target_field if isinstance(target_field, FieldInfo) else None
368|                        env_val = self.decode_complex_value(last_key, field_info, env_val)  # type: ignore
369|                    except ValueError:
370|                        if not allow_json_failure:
371|                            raise
372|            if isinstance(env_var, dict) and (
373|                last_key not in env_var or not isinstance(env_val, EnvNoneType) or env_var[last_key] == {}
374|            ):
375|                env_var[last_key] = self._coerce_env_val_strict(target_field, env_val)
376|        return result

378|    def _coerce_env_val_strict(self, field: FieldInfo | None, value: Any) -> Any:
379|        """
380|        Coerce environment string values based on field annotation if model config is `strict=True`
381|        or if the field annotation contains strict-annotated types (e.g. Optional[StrictBool]).
382|
383|        Args:
384|            field: The field.
385|            value: The value to coerce.
386|
387|        Returns:
388|            The coerced value if successful, otherwise the original value.
389|        """
390|        try:
391|            should_coerce = self.config.get('strict')
392|            if isinstance(field, FieldInfo):
393|                annotation, metadata = _get_field_annotation_and_metadata(field)
394|                if not should_coerce:
395|                    should_coerce = (
396|                        is_union_origin(get_origin(annotation)) and _union_has_strict_types(annotation)
397|                    ) or _literal_has_numeric_enum(annotation)
398|            if should_coerce and isinstance(value, str) and isinstance(field, FieldInfo):
399|                if value == self.env_parse_none_str:
400|                    return value
401|                has_json = any(isinstance(md, Json) for md in metadata)  # type: ignore[misc]
402|                if not has_json and not _annotation_contains_types(annotation, (Json,), is_instance=True):
403|                    try:
404|                        return TypeAdapter(cast('Any', field.annotation)).validate_python(value)
405|                    except ValidationError:
406|                        # Try JSON decoding as fallback (e.g. 'true' -> True for StrictBool)
407|                        decoded = json.loads(value)
408|                        if not isinstance(decoded, str):
409|                            return TypeAdapter(cast('Any', field.annotation)).validate_python(decoded)
410|                        raise
411|        except (ValidationError, json.JSONDecodeError):
412|            # Allow validation error to be raised at time of instantiation
413|            pass
414|        return value

419|            f'env_prefix_len={self.env_prefix_len!r})'

277|def _get_member_field(model_cls: type[Any], name: str) -> FieldInfo | None:
278|    """Get a field of a discriminated union member: a model, a pydantic dataclass or a stdlib dataclass.
279|
280|    Returns ``None`` if a stdlib dataclass field's annotation can't be resolved, e.g. when it names a class that
281|    is only in a local scope, so a `Field()` in its `Annotated` metadata is then not found.
282|    """
283|    if _is_model_or_dataclass(model_cls):
284|        return _get_model_fields(model_cls).get(name)
285|    # Pydantic doesn't attach `__pydantic_fields__` to a stdlib dataclass, so find the `FieldInfo` itself:
286|    # `Field()` is kept as the dataclass field's default, or in its `Annotated` metadata.
287|    dc_field = next((f for f in dataclass_fields(model_cls) if f.name == name), None)
288|    if dc_field is None:
289|        return None
290|    if isinstance(dc_field.default, FieldInfo):
291|        return dc_field.default
292|    # Resolve this field's annotation alone, as another field may name a class that is only in a local scope.
293|    # `typing` can't evaluate a single annotation, so it is put on a class created in the module of the class
294|    # declaring the field, which may be a base in another module.
295|    try:
296|        # On Python 3.14+ reading `__annotations__` evaluates them, so it can raise `NameError` too
297|        owner = next((c for c in model_cls.__mro__ if name in getattr(c, '__annotations__', {})), model_cls)
298|        annotations_holder = type(
299|            owner.__name__, (), {'__module__': owner.__module__, '__annotations__': {name: dc_field.type}}
300|        )
301|        hint = get_type_hints(annotations_holder, localns=dict(vars(owner)), include_extras=True)[name]
302|    except NameError:
303|        return None
304|    return next((m for m in get_args(hint)[1:] if isinstance(m, FieldInfo)), None)

308|    """Get the keys that can hold the discriminator value of a discriminated union member: its name and alias."""

313|def _get_nested_discriminators(annotation: Any) -> list[str] | None:
314|    """Get the discriminators nested inside a discriminated union's annotation.
315|
316|    A member can be guarded by more than one discriminator, e.g. in
317|    ``Annotated[Annotated[BlackCat | WhiteCat, Discriminator('color')] | Dog, Discriminator('pet_type')]``
318|    reaching ``BlackCat`` requires both ``pet_type='cat'`` and ``color='black'``. Each one has to keep the
319|    default's value for its default to still apply.
320|
321|    A nested discriminator can be given as ``Discriminator(...)`` or ``Field(discriminator=...)``.
322|
323|    Returns ``None`` if a nested discriminator can't be resolved to a field name (i.e. it is callable), as
324|    the member it selects can't be looked up in the incoming value.
325|    """
326|    from pydantic import Discriminator
327|
328|    discriminators: list[str] = []
329|    for arg in get_args(annotation):
330|        if arg is type(None):
331|            continue
332|        for metadata in get_args(arg)[1:]:
333|            # A nested discriminator is set either with `Discriminator(...)` or `Field(discriminator=...)`
334|            if isinstance(metadata, FieldInfo):
335|                discriminator = _get_discriminator(metadata)
336|            elif isinstance(metadata, Discriminator):
337|                discriminator = metadata.discriminator
338|            else:
339|                continue
340|            if discriminator is None:
341|                continue
342|            if not isinstance(discriminator, str):
343|                return None
344|            discriminators.append(discriminator)
345|        nested = _get_nested_discriminators(arg)
346|        if nested is None:
347|            return None
348|        discriminators.extend(nested)
349|    return discriminators

352|class DefaultSettingsSource(PydanticBaseSettingsSource):
353|    """
354|    Source class for loading default object values.
355|
356|    Args:

359|            Defaults to `False`.

362|    def __init__(
363|        self,
364|        settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
365|        nested_model_default_partial_update: bool | None = None,
366|        _init_state: InitState | None = None,
367|    ):
368|        super().__init__(settings_cls, _init_state)
369|        self.defaults: dict[str, Any] = {}

371|        # its value, and the default's value
372|        self._discriminator_tags: dict[str, list[tuple[tuple[str, ...], Any]]] = {}
373|        self.nested_model_default_partial_update = (
374|            nested_model_default_partial_update
375|            if nested_model_default_partial_update is not None
376|            else self.config.get('nested_model_default_partial_update', False)
377|        )
378|        if self.nested_model_default_partial_update:
379|            validate_by_alias = _validate_by_alias_enabled(self.config)
380|            for field_name, field_info in settings_cls.model_fields.items():
381|                _warn_if_field_info_incomplete(field_info, field_name, self._init_state)
382|                discriminator = _get_discriminator(field_info)
383|                if callable(discriminator):
384|                    # The member selected by a callable discriminator can't be looked up in the incoming value
385|                    continue
386|                nested = _get_nested_discriminators(field_info.annotation) if discriminator is not None else []
387|                if nested is None:
388|                    # Same for a nested callable discriminator
389|                    continue
390|                alias_names, *_ = _get_alias_names(field_name, field_info, validate_by_alias=validate_by_alias)
391|                preferred_alias = alias_names[0]
392|                if is_dataclass(type(field_info.default)):
393|                    self.defaults[preferred_alias] = asdict(field_info.default)
394|                elif is_model_class(type(field_info.default)):
395|                    self.defaults[preferred_alias] = field_info.default.model_dump()
396|                if discriminator is not None and preferred_alias in self.defaults:
397|                    default_cls = type(field_info.default)
398|                    self._discriminator_tags[preferred_alias] = [
399|                        (_get_discriminator_keys(default_cls, name), getattr(field_info.default, name, None))
400|                        for name in (discriminator, *nested)

404|        # Nothing to do here. Only implement the return statement to make mypy happy
405|        return None, '', False

407|    def __call__(self) -> dict[str, Any]:

428|    Source class for loading values provided during settings class initialization.

431|    def __init__(
432|        self,
433|        settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
434|        init_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
435|        nested_model_default_partial_update: bool | None = None,
436|        _init_state: InitState | None = None,

445|            return name if case_sensitive else name.lower()

448|        init_kwarg_names = set(init_kwargs.keys())
449|        # Map each normalized name to all provided keys sharing it, so field aliases can
450|        # be matched without losing the original key used to look up the value. A 1-to-many
451|        # mapping is required because case_sensitive=False can collapse distinct keys
452|        # (e.g. ``TeSt`` and ``TEST``) onto the same normalized name.
453|        normalized_provided: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
454|        for key in init_kwargs:
455|            normalized_provided.setdefault(normalize(key), []).append(key)
456|        for field_name, field_info in settings_cls.model_fields.items():
457|            _warn_if_field_info_incomplete(field_info, field_name, self._init_state)
458|            # Canonical (case-preserving) alias names determine the output key, so the value
459|            # still matches pydantic's validation aliases, which are always case-sensitive.
460|            canonical_alias_names, *_ = _get_alias_names(field_name, field_info, validate_by_alias=validate_by_alias)

462|            match_alias_names, *_ = _get_alias_names(
463|                field_name, field_info, case_sensitive=case_sensitive, validate_by_alias=validate_by_alias
464|            )
465|            # When populate_by_name is True, allow using the field name as an input key,
466|            # but normalize to the preferred alias to keep keys consistent across sources.
467|            matchable_names = list(match_alias_names)
468|            if include_name:
469|                name = normalize(field_name)
470|                if name not in matchable_names:
471|                    matchable_names.append(name)
472|            # All provided keys matching this field, in matchable_names preference order
473|            # (aliases first, then the field name). Only keys not yet consumed by an
474|            # earlier field are considered.
475|            matched_keys = [
476|                original
477|                for name in matchable_names
478|                if name in normalized_provided
479|                for original in normalized_provided[name]
480|                if original in init_kwarg_names

482|            if matched_keys:

485|                # so they are not re-added as extras.

491|        self.init_kwargs.update({key: val for key, val in init_kwargs.items() if key in init_kwarg_names})

493|        self.nested_model_default_partial_update = (
494|            nested_model_default_partial_update
495|            if nested_model_default_partial_update is not None
496|            else self.config.get('nested_model_default_partial_update', False)
497|        )

510|    def __repr__(self) -> str:

624|                SUB_sub_SuB: SubSubSub

627|                VAL1: str
628|                SUB_sub: SubSub

631|                nested: Sub
632|
633|                model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_nested_delimiter='__')

637|            _replace_field_names_case_insensitively(

871|    def _consume_object_or_array(self, item: str, merged_list: list[str]) -> str:
872|        count = 1

875|        for consumed in range(1, len(item)):
876|            if item[consumed] == '"' and item[consumed - 1] != '\\':
877|                in_str = not in_str
878|            elif in_str:
879|                continue
880|            elif item[consumed] in ('{', '['):
881|                count += 1
882|            elif item[consumed] in ('}', ']'):
883|                count -= 1
884|                if item[consumed] == close_delim and count == 0:
885|                    merged_list.append(item[: consumed + 1])

889|    def _consume_string_or_number(self, item: str, merged_list: list[str], merge_type: type[Any] | None) -> str:
890|        consumed = 0 if merge_type is not str else len(item)
891|        is_find_end_quote = False
892|        while consumed < len(item):
893|            if item[consumed] == '"' and (consumed == 0 or item[consumed - 1] != '\\'):
894|                is_find_end_quote = not is_find_end_quote
895|            if not is_find_end_quote and item[consumed] == ',':
896|                break
897|            consumed += 1
898|        if is_find_end_quote:
899|            raise SettingsError('Mismatched quotes')
900|        val_string = item[:consumed].strip()
901|        if merge_type in (list, str):
902|            try:
903|                float(val_string)
904|            except ValueError:
905|                if val_string == self.cli_parse_none_str:
906|                    val_string = 'null'
907|                if val_string not in ('true', 'false', 'null') and not val_string.startswith('"'):
908|                    val_string = f'"{val_string}"'
909|            merged_list.append(val_string)
910|        else:
911|            key, val = (kv for kv in val_string.split('=', 1))
912|            if key.startswith('"') and not key.endswith('"') and not val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"'):
913|                raise ValueError(f'Dictionary key=val parameter is a quoted string: {val_string}')
914|            key, val = key.strip('"'), val.strip('"')
915|            merged_list.append(json.dumps({key: val}))
916|        return item[consumed:]

1016|    def _lower_option_names(self, parser: ArgumentParser, args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
1017|        """Lowercase the options in `args` that `parser` registers, keeping every other arg as typed.
1018|

1020|        """

1022|            name: subparser
1023|            for action in parser._actions
1024|            if isinstance(action, _SubParsersAction)
1025|            for name, subparser in action.choices.items()
1026|        }
1027|        flag_prefix = rf'\{self.cli_flag_prefix_char}{{1,2}}'
1028|        lowered: list[str] = []
1029|        # how many of the next args are values of the last option, `None` for any number
1030|        values_left: int | None = 0
1031|        for index, arg in enumerate(args):
1032|            if arg == '--':
1033|                # everything after '--' is a positional value, not an option
1034|                return lowered + args[index:]
1035|            matched = re.match(rf'^({flag_prefix}[^\s=]+)(.*)', arg)
1036|            if not matched or _NEGATIVE_NUMBER.match(arg):
1037|                if values_left != 0:
1038|                    if values_left is not None:
1039|                        values_left -= 1
1040|                elif arg in subparsers:
1041|                    return lowered + [arg] + self._lower_option_names(subparsers[arg], args[index + 1 :])
1042|                lowered.append(arg)
1043|                continue
1044|            arg, action = self._lower_option(matched.group(1), matched.group(2), parser._option_string_actions)
1045|            values_left = _count_option_values(action)
1046|            lowered.append(arg)

1049|    def _lower_option(self, flag: str, rest: str, option_actions: Mapping[str, Action]) -> tuple[str, Action | None]:
1050|        """Lowercase a registered option, or the short options in a token like `-P80` or `-VP80`.
1051|
1052|        Returns the arg and, when its value isn't attached, the action that takes the following args as values.
1053|        """
1054|        if flag.lower() in option_actions:
1055|            return flag.lower() + rest, None if rest else option_actions[flag.lower()]

1057|        arg = flag + rest
1058|        if arg.startswith(prefix * 2):
1059|            # not a registered option, keep the arg as typed
1060|            return arg, None
1061|        for index in range(1, len(arg)):
1062|            action = option_actions.get(prefix + arg[index].lower())

1065|                return arg, None
1066|            if action.nargs != 0:

1455|    def _get_arg_names(
1456|        self,
1457|        arg: _CliArg,
1458|        subcommand_prefix: str,
1459|        alias_prefixes: list[str],
1460|        added_args: list[str],
1461|        discriminator_vals: dict[str, set[Any]],

1471|                    self.cli_kebab_case,
1472|                )
1473|                if arg_name not in added_args:

1480|                    arg_names.extend(alias for alias in alias_list if alias not in added_args)
1481|
1482|        tags: set[Any] = set()

1486|                arg.field_info.annotation,
1487|                (Literal,),
1488|                is_include_origin=True,

1628|        metavar = ','.join(args)

1633|    def _metavar_format_recurse(self, obj: Any) -> str:
1634|        """Pretty metavar representation of a type. Adapts logic from `pydantic._repr.display_as_type`."""
1635|        obj = _strip_annotated(obj)
1636|        if _is_function(obj):
1637|            # If function is locally defined use __name__ instead of __qualname__
1638|            return obj.__name__ if '<locals>' in obj.__qualname__ else obj.__qualname__
1639|        if obj is ...:
1640|            return '...'
1641|        if isinstance(obj, Representation):
1642|            return repr(obj)
1643|        if isinstance(obj, typing.ForwardRef) or typing_objects.is_typealiastype(obj):
1644|            return str(obj)
1645|
1646|        if not isinstance(obj, (_typing_base, _WithArgsTypes, type)):
1647|            obj = obj.__class__
1648|
1649|        origin = get_origin(obj)
1650|        if is_union_origin(origin):
1651|            return self._metavar_format_choices(list(map(self._metavar_format_recurse, self._get_modified_args(obj))))
1652|        if typing_objects.is_literal(origin):
1653|            return self._metavar_format_choices(list(map(str, self._get_modified_args(obj))))
1654|        if _lenient_issubclass(obj, Enum):
1655|            return self._metavar_format_choices(
1656|                [_CliArg.get_kebab_case(name, self.cli_kebab_case == 'all') for name in obj.__members__]
1657|            )
1658|        if isinstance(obj, _WithArgsTypes):
1659|            return self._metavar_format_choices(
1660|                list(map(self._metavar_format_recurse, self._get_modified_args(obj))),
1661|                obj_qualname=obj.__qualname__ if hasattr(obj, '__qualname__') else str(obj),
1662|            )
1663|        if obj is type(None):
1664|            return self.cli_parse_none_str
1665|        if is_model_class(obj) or is_pydantic_dataclass(obj):
1666|            return (
1667|                self._metavar_format_recurse(_get_model_fields(obj)['root'].annotation)
1668|                if getattr(obj, '__pydantic_root_model__', False)
1669|                else 'JSON'
1670|            )
1671|        if isinstance(obj, type):
1672|            return obj.__qualname__
1673|        return repr(obj).replace('typing.', '').replace('typing_extensions.', '')
1674|

1890|                sub_args = self._serialized_args(
1891|                    model_default,
1892|                    list_style=list_style,
1893|                    dict_style=dict_style,
1894|                    positionals_first=positionals_first,
1895|                    _is_submodel=True,
1896|                )

1898|                positional_args += sub_args['positional']
1899|                subcommand_args += sub_args['subcommand']
1900|                unknown_args += sub_args['unknown']

34|        settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
35|        secrets_dir: PathType | None = None,
36|        case_sensitive: bool | None = None,
37|        env_prefix: str | None = None,
38|        env_prefix_target: EnvPrefixTarget | None = None,
39|        env_ignore_empty: bool | None = None,
40|        env_parse_none_str: str | None = None,
41|        env_parse_enums: bool | None = None,
42|        _init_state: InitState | None = None,
43|    ) -> None:
44|        super().__init__(
45|            settings_cls,
46|            case_sensitive,
47|            env_prefix,
48|            env_prefix_target,
49|            env_ignore_empty,
50|            env_parse_none_str,
51|            env_parse_enums,
52|            _init_state,
53|        )
54|        self.secrets_dir = secrets_dir if secrets_dir is not None else self.config.get('secrets_dir')
55|
56|    def __call__(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
57|        """
58|        Build fields from "secrets" files.
59|        """
60|        secrets: dict[str, str | None] = {}
61|
62|        if self.secrets_dir is None:
63|            return secrets
64|
65|        secrets_dirs = [self.secrets_dir] if isinstance(self.secrets_dir, (str, os.PathLike)) else self.secrets_dir
66|        secrets_paths = [Path(p).expanduser() for p in secrets_dirs]
67|        self.secrets_paths = []
68|
69|        for path in secrets_paths:
70|            if not path.exists():
71|                # No `stacklevel`: this source is reached at different depths — via
72|                # `Settings()` (through `_settings_build_values`) or by instantiating
73|                # the source directly — so no fixed value attributes the warning to
74|                # user code in both cases.
75|                warnings.warn(f'directory "{path}" does not exist')  # noqa: B028
76|            else:
77|                self.secrets_paths.append(path)
78|
79|        if not len(self.secrets_paths):
80|            return secrets
81|
82|        for path in self.secrets_paths:
83|            if not path.is_dir():
84|                raise SettingsError(f'secrets_dir must reference a directory, not a {path_type_label(path)}')
85|
86|        return super().__call__()
87|
88|    @classmethod
89|    def find_case_path(cls, dir_path: Path, file_name: str, case_sensitive: bool) -> Path | None:
90|        """
91|        Find a file within path's directory matching filename, optionally ignoring case.
92|
93|        Args:
94|            dir_path: Directory path.
95|            file_name: File name.
96|            case_sensitive: Whether to search for file name case sensitively.
97|
98|        Returns:
99|            Whether file path or `None` if file does not exist in directory.
100|        """
101|        for f in dir_path.iterdir():
102|            if f.name == file_name or (not case_sensitive and f.name.lower() == file_name.lower()):
103|                return f
104|        return None
105|
106|    def get_field_value(self, field: FieldInfo, field_name: str) -> tuple[Any, str, bool]:
107|        """
108|        Gets the value for field from secret file and a flag to determine whether value is complex.
109|
110|        Args:
111|            field: The field.
112|            field_name: The field name.
113|
114|        Returns:
115|            A tuple that contains the value (`None` if the file does not exist), key, and
116|                a flag to determine whether value is complex.
117|        """
118|
119|        debug = _settings_debug_enabled() and logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)
120|
121|        for field_key, env_name, value_is_complex in self._extract_field_info(field, field_name):
122|            # paths reversed to match the last-wins behaviour of `env_file`
123|            for secrets_path in reversed(self.secrets_paths):
124|                path = self.find_case_path(secrets_path, env_name, self.case_sensitive)
125|                if not path:
126|                    # path does not exist, we currently don't return a warning for this
127|                    if debug:
128|                        logger.debug('Secret file not found, skipping: %s', (secrets_path / env_name).resolve())
129|                    continue
130|
131|                if path.is_file():
132|                    if debug:
133|                        logger.debug('Loading secret file: %s', path.resolve())
134|                    # Explicit encoding: `read_text()` would otherwise decode with the
135|                    # locale encoding, so a UTF-8 secret is corrupted on a non-UTF-8
136|                    # Windows code page (silently, when every byte happens to map).
137|                    return path.read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip(), field_key, value_is_complex
138|                warnings.warn(
139|                    f'attempted to load secret file "{path}" but found a {path_type_label(path)} instead.',
140|                    stacklevel=4,
141|                )
142|
143|        return None, field_key, value_is_complex
144|
145|    def __repr__(self) -> str:
146|        return f'{self.__class__.__name__}(secrets_dir={self.secrets_dir!r})'
